title: LibRedirect Mobile routing manifest (schemaVersion 1)
description: Structural validation for the signed routing manifest the app consumes. Cross-record constraints that cannot be expressed here (global route-id uniqueness, global host uniqueness, private/local instance host rejection, custom-scheme allowlist membership) are enforced by tools/validate-routes.ts semantic validation, not by this schema.

schemaVersion.description: This file only validates schemaVersion 1 manifests. A future breaking change to the manifest shape ships as schemaVersion 2 with its own schema file; old app builds reject any schemaVersion they do not recognize.

revision.description: Single global monotonically increasing counter, independent of schemaVersion. The app rejects any manifest whose revision is lower than the currently active one.

id.description: Lowercase kebab-case identifier. Used as a persistent settings key on the client, so it must not be repurposed for a different route/frontend once published.

hostname.description: Exact hostname to match, lowercase, at least two labels. No wildcards and no implicit normalization: every host variant a route should match (www., m., youtu.be, ...) must be listed explicitly.

instanceOrigin.description: HTTPS origin only: scheme + host + optional port, no path/query/fragment. This is the literal value substituted for {instance} and for the replaced origin in the replace-origin strategy. Rejection of private/local/loopback hosts (localhost, 127.0.0.1, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, ::1, ...) is semantic validation, not expressible as a single regex here.

hosts.description: Every host in this list must be globally unique across the entire manifest: a host may belong to at most one route.

hostPatterns.description: Anchored, hostname-only patterns used for upstream services with wildcard subdomains. Patterns are validated against the app's safe subset before activation.

frontends.description: Frontend ids only need to be unique within this route, not across the manifest.

strategy.description: Substitutes the selected instance's origin for the matched URL's origin. Path, query, and fragment pass through unchanged.

output.description: May reference exactly {instance}, {path}, {query:NAME}, and {fragment}. The full placeholder grammar (which forms are valid, how each is percent-encoded on substitution) is specified in the manifest-format plan artifact and implemented independently by tools/validate-routes.ts and the Android template strategy — this schema only bounds length and rejects control characters.

scheme.description: Destination app URI scheme (no trailing ':'). The matched URL is rewritten to '{scheme}://{originalUrl}' verbatim; there is no instance to select. Whether the app actually honors a given scheme at runtime is a Phase 7 app-side allowlist decision, not something this schema enforces.

customSchemeFrontend.description: No 'instances' field: custom-scheme wraps the original URL for a destination app, it does not pick among hosted instances.

passthroughFrontend.description: No 'instances' field. Lets a route expose an explicit 'use the original site' choice alongside its other frontends, e.g. in a frontend selector UI, rather than requiring the user to fall back to a client-side exception.
